_note: DELIBERATE-DIVERGENCE REGISTRY. Some differences between a bot's language files are INTENTIONAL, owner-approved decisions -- not drift. This file is the machine-checkable record of them. `/sync-check` loads it and reports a covered difference as 'EXPECTED (registered divergence)' instead of drift; an UNREGISTERED difference in language-agnostic content is what gets flagged. `/update-prompt` and `/port-feature` MUST add an entry here -- in the same change as the prompt edit and the CHANGELOG entry -- whenever they knowingly apply a change to some languages of a sync family and not others, or otherwise suspend the master->mirror sync rule. No entry = the next audit will 'correct' the divergence and silently undo an owner decision. An entry is a NARROW carve-out (specific targets, languages, sections and tokens), never a blanket licence for a language to differ; everything in `still_must_match` is audited normally. Lives next to agents.json because it is fleet data read by /sync-check, /update-prompt, /port-feature and raya/regression/static_regression.py -- not skill prose. Schema notes: .claude/skills/sync-check/reference/n-language-parity.md

_schema.id: stable kebab-case key; cited verbatim in audit reports
_schema.bot: the bot/agent the divergence belongs to (KKB, DKB, Maya, purple-dots, ...)
_schema.sync_family: 'bot · direction · variant' -- scopes the entry to ONE sync family; files in other families are not mirrors of each other
_schema.targets: raya/agents.json target ids this divergence applies to
_schema.master_language: the family's master language at the time of approval
_schema.languages_affected: language codes that legitimately differ from the master
_schema.scope: the sections/lines that legitimately differ. Each item: section (heading, matched by intent not exact string), kind (persona|spoken-line|rule), what (plain English), contains[] (tokens a script can match inside the actual delta)
_schema.why: the owner's reason, in plain English
_schema.approved_by: the human who decided, and how (explicit instruction / email approval)
_schema.changelog_ref: the CHANGELOG.md entry that records the edit
_schema.still_must_match: everything this entry does NOT excuse -- audited normally
_schema.not_applied_to: sibling targets deliberately left alone (stops scope creep)
_schema.review_on: optional; after this date the entry must be re-confirmed or it is reported as a registry gap
_schema.expires: optional hard expiry; after it, the divergence is drift again
_schema._match_rule: A difference is EXPECTED only if ALL hold: (1) the file's target id is in `targets` and its family matches `sync_family`; (2) the file's language is in `languages_affected`; (3) the differing section matches a scope[].section by intent; (4) the delta text contains at least one of that scope item's `contains` tokens. Anything else is UNREGISTERED = drift. If a scope item's `contains` tokens are NO LONGER present in the covered files, the divergence was undone -- report a registry gap / possible silent revert and ask the owner; do not delete the entry and do not silently re-apply it.

The Hindi Signals twins intentionally keep the institution-only persona ('You are काम की बात') with no personal name.

scope.section: Call Introduction Rules → Introduction Script (fixed opening line)
scope.what: The fixed opening line carries one extra short sentence, 'ನಾನು ಮಾಯಾ.', inserted after 'ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ.' and before the existing institutional welcome. Everything else in the greeting -- including the recording disclosure and its position -- is byte-identical to before. The Hindi opening line has no equivalent self-naming sentence.

Kannada-only intro-turn rules that exist because of the name: (a) 'give your name once in this intro turn, never repeat it in later turns' (guards the repetition failure class); (b) the identity anchor reads that the NAME TOGETHER WITH the city-administration initiative is the whole identity -- the Hindi twins still read that the institutional anchor is the entire identity, which would contradict a personal name; (c) an explicit guard that being named ಮಾಯಾ does not make the agent a private individual, an agent, or a company representative.
contains: Give your name once, in this intro turn
does not make you a private individual

divergences.why: Feature request from the owner: the KKB Kannada bots should be called Maya and state that name in their introduction. Applied to the Kannada Signals pair ONLY, at the owner's explicit instruction -- the Hindi Signals twins and BOTH legacy Kannada bots keep the institution-only intro with no personal name. For this pair the normal 'Hindi is source of truth, mirror to Kannada' rule was consciously suspended for a language-specific persona choice. A /sync-check WILL see a persona-line, opening-line and intro-turn-rule difference between KKB Hindi Signals and KKB Kannada Signals: that is EXPECTED, not drift. ('Maya' is also the name of the separate Maya agent -- Hindi-only, UP campus recruitment, ${college_name}. Different agents, different prompts, different uuids; the shared first name is intentional and has no functional coupling.) Extended 2026-09-10 to the Kannada SLIM twin (kkb-kn-signals-slim): the slim bots are latency A/B twins of the production bots, so the Kannada slim must speak with the same persona name as the Kannada bot it is being compared against — otherwise the A/B measures two different bots.
